_readme: THE LIVE TO-DO LIST, AS DATA. This file is the source. to-do.md's ranked table is
GENERATED from it by `npm run to-do`, and the Handbook's ranking control reads it.
Edit here — an edit to that table is overwritten.
A list saved from the control comes back with `npm run to-do -- <file>`. It is
validated against the five fields first, and an item Mike settles is NOT removed
until its closure is written on to-do-done-and-parked.md — the command applies
nothing at all until then. An item gone from both pages is an item nobody knows
existed.
FORMATTING IS THE SCRIPT'S. Applying a saved list rewrites this file with two-space
JSON, so do not hand-tune the layout; it will not survive.
Every item must carry all five fields the list's own rules demand — score, why,
risk, askedBy, touches — and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build if one
is missing. That guard is the whole reason this file exists: an item missing a
field is a note, and notes are what produced two pieces of unrequested work on
ORDER IS MIKE'S RANKING. The array order is the order on screen. It is not
computed from the score, and it must never be re-sorted by a script or a session.
Where his order and the score disagree, his order wins and the score stays
visible so the disagreement is on the page.
KIND — 'defect' or 'feature', and it is a GATE, not a label. A defect is something
that already exists being wrong, missing, unverified or unmaintainable. A feature is a
new capability, page, screen or behaviour. tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js FAILS THE BUILD
on a feature whose askedBy.ours is true — a new thing nobody outside asked for cannot be
filed at all. A defect we found ourselves still can, because Mike never asked us to stop
reporting bugs; he asked us to stop inventing work.
SCORE — 5 security/privacy/data integrity · 4 the user is worse off · 3 helps
sell the package · 2 robustness · 1 internal only · 0 is not filed, it is
deleted with its code.
askedBy.ours = true means NOBODY OUTSIDE ASKED. It is not a defect to record it;
it is a defect to hide it. An item that cannot name Mike or a named outsider has
to justify itself.
orderSource: the Handbook ranking control (scripts/handbook-shell.html), saved by Mike on 2026-08-15. It replaced design/mockups/to-do-list-table.html, which set the order before it.

items.name: The 21 branches that still name a page nobody can open
items.why: Of the 55 recommendations across the logic tables, 28 lose text to the template gate because they name a page that does not exist in the 291-record library. Seven were the Get Seminar branches, fixed 2026-08-15 once Mike named the real page (Design & Deliver). The other 21 sit in the fmc_, cas_, fbp_ and ol_ tables and nobody has looked at them.
items.risk: 21 branches of Mike's own coaching are cut back or withheld before they reach an adviser. The gate is behaving correctly; the content names tools that are not there. Each one is advice an adviser is not getting, and nothing on screen says so.

askedBy.detail: 2026-08-15 — "put them in the list of to dos", after being shown that the seven Seminar branches were seven of twenty-eight. Found by us; filed on his instruction.

items.touches: data/logic_trees.json, the Mentor Hub logic tables, and the Template Check screen where the real page names are settled.
items.note: RANKED LAST DELIBERATELY, and it scores 4. Mike's ruling the same day: clear the technical and feature work first so the master team can start UAT testing, THEN double back to wording and document-title alignment. This is wording and title alignment. The pattern is proven and cheap once a name is known — the Seminar seven took five words and a seven-line diff — but each of the 21 needs the REAL page name, and that is Mike's to give, never a developer's to rule on. Put the actual sentences in front of him, not the label: that is what unblocked 2.3 after four sessions. 🔴 A SECOND STEP WAS FOUND ON 2026-08-26 AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL. Measuring the empty `templates[]` arrays (raised as 4.51, closed the same day) showed that 22 of the branches with an EMPTY array name their templates in the recommendation PROSE instead — "Use Design & Deliver template", "Use De Bono's 6 Hats" — and those prose names are this item's own missing documents, in the same trees (35, cas_, fbp_). The consequence nobody had recorded: `walkLogicTree` in server/utils/logicTrees.js L1037 reads ONLY `node.templates`, never the prose. So the tree's judgement about which tool fits reaches the ADVISER as a sentence and never reaches the RANKING ENGINE, where it is meant to act as the tie-breaker. When the search content is updated and the names resolve, populating `templates[]` on those 22 branches is a required second step — the sentences alone leave the engine exactly as blind as it is now. ⚠ AND IT CANNOT BE DONE FIRST: `validateLogicTreeReferences` scans `nodes[].templates` and hard-fails under VA_STRICT_CONTENT, so writing a name into the array before the document exists turns a silent gap into a broken build.
items.comment: 2026-08-25 - WAITING ON MIKE, AND THE WHOLE LIST IS WRITTEN DOWN: design/LOGIC-TABLE-TEMPLATES-NEEDED.md, and as a page at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9a5bf350-befd-444f-b574-4d806200420f. 19 branches across three logic tables (CA Firm Strategy 5, Firm Board Pack 7, Leadership & Partner Development 7) name 23 documents data/templates.json does not hold. Mike says the documents exist and will update the search content, then pick this up. Nothing to do here until he does. MATCHING IGNORES CASE AND PUNCTUATION, so some may already be solved - 'Demings Volatility' is published and matches "Deming's Theory of Volatility"; '6 Hats' matches "De Bono's 6 Hats". A sentence dies if ANY name in it is missing, and four branches name two. 'Psyche Errors' and 'Team AI' may be concepts rather than documents - if so the fix is to reword the sentence and no page is needed. WAS 21, NOW 19: COI Development pt1 and pt2 were published all along and the name scanner was cutting the title at the lowercase 'pt' (fixed in 48265ac). When the search content is updated, re-run the gate over all 55 recommendations - the command is in the reference file. Today: 36 whole / 6 partial / 13 withheld, pinned in tests/unit/recommendationGate.test.js.

items.name: A screen can show one row when 67 exist, and say nothing
items.why: The mentor's Advisory Distinctions tab showed 1 distinction when the shipped set is 67. A local, git-ignored dev file (data/dev-platform-distinctions.json) is deliberately preferred over the committed seed when there is no database, and one stale test row in it shadowed all 67 — with nothing on screen saying so.
items.risk: Anyone developing, demoing or reviewing reads what is on screen as the real platform set. It cost most of a session to diagnose, and the same pattern applies to every dev-JSON fallback in the app, not just this one.

askedBy.detail: He spotted it himself on the Mentor Hub, 2026-08-16 — 'the advisory distinctions ... no longer appear to be linked and working at mentor level'. Diagnosed the same session.

items.touches: server/utils/platformDistinctions.js and every other dev-JSON fallback (firmDistinctions, quizzes, coaching, currency); the Mentor Hub Advisory Distinctions tab.
items.note: THE LOCAL SYMPTOM IS FIXED BY DELETING THE FILE — Mike was given the command on 2026-08-16 because the AI's own safety guard refused the deletion. THE ITEM IS THE UNDERLYING FAULT, not that file: a screen served from a dev fallback must SAY it is, e.g. 'showing local dev data — 67 shipped rows are being shadowed'. Same family as 4.16 and the same lesson: the content was there, the screen was there, and nothing connected the two or admitted the gap. Verify the fix by loading the tab with and without the local file, not by reading the loader.

items.name: A template's tutorial video gets attached to a calculator that shares its name
items.why: server/utils/videoInjector.js appends 'A 24-minute tutorial video is available in Advisor-e to help you prepare' after ANY bolded name that matches a template holding a video. Since 2026-08-22 the AI may also name a CALCULATION MODEL in its answer, and two model names are also template names: Working Capital Cycle and Quick Position. Seen live: the calculator line read 'Working Capital Cycle — ... open it at /business-performance-report' followed immediately by the 24-minute video sentence. The video is real, and it belongs to the TEMPLATE of that name, not to the calculator page the advisor was just pointed at.
items.risk: Small and specific: an advisor goes looking for a tutorial about a calculator screen and finds a video about a different thing with the same name. It is not a fabrication — the video exists — which is what makes it easy to miss. It cannot be fixed in the prompt: the injector runs AFTER the AI has written the answer and matches on bold text alone, so telling the AI to write differently only moves the problem.

askedBy.detail: Found 2026-08-22 while testing item 4.32 against the running app. Raised rather than fixed in passing, because videoInjector is a shipped, tested utility and the honest options differ in cost — see the note.

items.touches: server/utils/videoInjector.js and its test, or data/report-model-summaries.json if the answer is to rename. Nothing in the prompts.
items.note: 🔴 THE PROMPT CANNOT FIX THIS, and an earlier attempt made things worse — instructing the AI not to bold a model name stripped the bold off the TEMPLATE name too, which is the very thing the injector reads. Reverted. ⚠ TWO HONEST OPTIONS, and they are not equivalent: (1) teach the injector to skip a line that carries a calculator page path, which is narrow and cheap but is pattern-matching on output shape; (2) accept it — the video is real and same-named material is arguably relevant, so nothing is untrue, just imprecise. There is a third that is NOT ours: renaming a model or a template is Mike's call and would ripple through the catalogue, the summaries and the template library. ⚠ AFFECTS EXACTLY TWO NAMES TODAY. Adding a model whose name matches a template widens it, which is worth knowing before the next one is catalogued. ⚠ FOUND IN THE SAME FILE 2026-08-26 (ACTIONS sweep, item 4.39): the injected sentence is hardcoded English on the BACKEND, so a non-English advisor gets one English line inside otherwise translated advice. `vue-i18n` does not exist on the backend, so the wording would have to be resolved another way. Pre-existing and separate from the name clash, but it is the same sentence in the same file — whoever opens videoInjector.js should settle both at once rather than touch it twice.

items.name: The to-do page’s hand-written half describes six finished items and misses ten live ones
items.why: `to-do.md` is a generated ranked table wrapped in hand-written per-item detail. Only the table is regenerated by `npm run to-do`; the prose is edited by hand and has drifted. As of 2026-08-24 it carries detail blocks for six items that are no longer live (2.9, 4.16, 4.19, 4.28, 4.29 and, until today, 4.7) and none at all for ten that are (4.15, 4.25, 4.27, 4.31, 4.33, 4.36–4.40). Only three live items have both. 4.7’s block also disagreed with its own data on score — the prose said 2, the JSON said 5.
items.risk: A reader cannot tell which half to believe, and the page is the human-readable front door to the work list. This is the same mechanism recorded in 2.9’s own closure: the generated table said one thing, the prose said another, and on 2026-08-24 a session read the wrong one and advised Mike to pick an item on a false basis. Nothing tests the prose against the data, so the drift is silent and grows every session.

askedBy.detail: Found 2026-08-24 while closing 4.7 — regenerating the table left a stale hand-written block behind, which exposed the wider gap. Nobody outside asked.

items.touches: `design/features/to-do.md` (the hand-written sections outside the generated region), and a guard in `tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js` comparing detail blocks to the live refs.
items.note: The fix is two jobs and the second is the one that lasts: remove or label the six stale blocks, then add the guard so this cannot recur. A guard that simply requires every detail block to name a live ref would have caught all six. Decide deliberately whether every live item MUST have a block — the four DONE/PARKED blocks (3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 4.8) are kept on purpose and carry an explicit label, so the rule is "labelled or live", not "live only".

items.name: Learn mode asks the advisor questions their own profile already answers
items.why: The advisor profile never reaches the Learn prompt. server/advisorEngine.js L3675 applies the profile only when mode is client or discover — Learn is excluded outright — and the profile block at L3661 is written in client-mode language ("do not ask the Phase 2 questions"), which means nothing to the Learn prompt. Meanwhile data/prompts/learn.txt L34-35 positively instructs the AI to ask "How would they describe their current skill or confidence level?" and "Have they had any training, coaching, or reading on this topic before?". The only carve-out (L80) is conditional on a Sales Process Decision Tree being present, not on the profile.
items.risk: The advisor fills in a profile and is then interviewed about what they just supplied. Mike caught this live: the AI asked, was told to read the profile, and apologised — proving it had held the profile all along. It reads as an app that does not remember, on the one screen meant to feel like coaching.

askedBy.detail: 2026-07-16 — found by Mike in a live Learn thread and audit-confirmed the same day. Logged in ACTIONS.md, which was frozen 2026-08-24 before it was picked up; re-verified against the code 2026-08-26 and unchanged.

items.touches: server/advisorEngine.js (the mode test at L3675 and the profile wording at L3661) and data/prompts/learn.txt (the "Where they are starting from" questions).
items.note: TWO CAUSES, AND FIXING ONE LEAVES THE DEFECT. Letting the profile through to Learn does not help while learn.txt still orders the question; removing the question does not help while the profile never arrives. Both halves, or neither. The carve-out to copy already exists at learn.txt L80 — it just keys off the wrong thing.

items.name: The hidden-marker change has never been run in a real conversation
items.why: Merged 2026-07-22 (PR #21, d791a9a): the AI declares its recommendations in a trailing [[TEMPLATES: ...]] marker that the engine holds back from the stream so it never reaches the advisor. 22 tests cover the parsing, the catalogue validation, the hold-back across awkward chunk splits and a truncated marker. No real conversation has ever been run against it, because this machine has no OPENAI_API_KEY and every advisor request fails at startup.
items.risk: Small but it is the last unproven step before UAT. What the tests cannot answer is whether the reply still streams smoothly and nothing odd surfaces at the end — a half-written marker appearing on screen for a moment would be visible to a tester and is exactly what no unit test can see.

askedBy.detail: Logged at the 2026-07-22 merge as the named residual of that change. Carried in ACTIONS.md until it was frozen 2026-08-24; re-checked 2026-08-26 and still unexercised.

items.touches: nothing — this is a live check, not a code change. server/advisorEngine.js holds the marker logic if the check fails.
items.note: CANNOT BE DONE ON THIS MACHINE — it needs one Virtual Advisor conversation somewhere an OpenAI key exists. Three things to look at, and it is a two-minute job for whoever has the key: (a) the reply streams normally, (b) no [[TEMPLATES text is ever visible, even briefly, (c) the session recommended templates look right on the Team Dashboard afterwards.
